title: The polynomial ring over a Noetherian N-2 domain is N-2
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] integral domain which is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], and let $R[x]$ be the polynomial ring in one variable $x$ over $R$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] (an integral domain). Then $R[x]$ is N-2: for every finite field extension $L$ of the fraction field $K(x)$ of $R[x]$, the integral closure of $R[x]$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $R[x]$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2, line 45411), second assertion

proof.text: Let A be the integral closure of R in Frac(R). Taking L=Frac(R) in IsN2 makes A finite over R. It is a Noetherian normal domain. The injectivity of R -> A follows by composing with A -> Frac(R).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2), proof of the second assertion, positive-characteristic argument

proof.text: Apply N-2 ascent along finite extensions of domains to R -> A: A is N-2 with its canonical fraction field.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2), proof of the second assertion, positive-characteristic argument

proof.text: A[x] is Noetherian, a domain, and normal. Work with its canonical fraction field directly, avoiding a separate RatFunc identification. This field has characteristic zero or prime characteristic.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2), proof of the second assertion, positive-characteristic argument

proof.text: In characteristic zero, the fraction field is perfect, so any finite extension is algebraic separable. Apply IsIntegralClosure.finite to A[x], its fraction field, the extension L and integralClosure A[x] L. This proves N-2 in characteristic zero without using separably generated extensions or transcendence bases.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2), proof of the second assertion, positive-characteristic argument

proof.text: In prime characteristic p, the normal Japanese domain A satisfies the new finite purely inseparable polynomial-closure lemma. For each finite purely inseparable L over Frac(A[x]), obtain Module.Finite A[x] (integralClosure A[x] L). This encapsulates the original Steps 5 to 8, with their full proof recorded at that node.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2), proof of the second assertion, positive-characteristic argument

proof.text: Apply the characteristic-p N-2 criterion to A[x] with the finiteness conclusion from the preceding step. Thus A[x] is N-2 in positive characteristic as well.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2), proof of the second assertion, positive-characteristic argument

proof.text: Show A[x] finite over R[x] from finite R-module generators s of A. Their constant polynomials span every constant polynomial by induction on R-linear combinations. Multiplication by X^n then puts every monomial in their R[x]-span; polynomial induction puts every polynomial in that span. Thus the finite set C(s) generates A[x]. The map R[x] -> A[x] is injective coefficientwise.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2), proof of the second assertion, positive-characteristic argument

proof.text: Apply N-2 descent along the finite injective domain extension R[x] -> A[x], with the canonical fraction fields on both sides. This gives precisely the original IsN2 R[x] (Frac(R[x])) conclusion.
